RF-mount lenses mount directly to the EOS R5 with no adapter required. All electronic functions are fully supported [2].

# Lens Mount Standards

Definitions and specifications for mount standards (RF, EF, EF-M, etc.): physical dimensions, electronic interfaces, flange distance, and which camera systems use each mount

Three Canon lens mount standards are relevant to camera-lens compatibility: **EF**, **RF**, and **EF-M**.

## Canon EF Mount

The EF (Electro-Focus) mount is Canon's legacy interchangeable-lens standard used by Canon EF lenses and EF-S lenses [3]. It is a wide-diameter bayonet mount with fully electronic lens communication (no mechanical aperture linkage). EF is the mount found on Canon's DSLR bodies and is the source mount in Canon's EF-to-EOS R adapter ecosystem (see adapters for the Canon Mount Adapter EF-EOS R) [3].

## Canon RF Mount

The RF mount is Canon's mirrorless standard introduced with the EOS R system [1]. RF lenses attach to Canon EOS R-series mirrorless camera bodies [1]. The RF mount features a shorter flange distance and a wider 54 mm internal diameter compared to EF, enabling a high-speed communication bus between lens and body. RF lenses are not mechanically compatible with EF or EF-M bodies; bridging requires an adapter (see adapters).

## Canon EF-M Mount

The EF-M mount is Canon's mirrorless standard for the EOS M camera system [2]. It is a smaller-diameter mount designed for compact EOS M bodies, distinct from both EF and RF [2]. EF-M lenses (such as the EF-M 22mm f/2 STM) are native to EOS M cameras and are not directly compatible with EOS R bodies or EF-mount DSLRs without an adapter.

| Mount | System | Lens type | Directly compatible bodies |

| EF-M | EOS M (mirrorless) | EF-M | EOS M-series (e.g., M50, M6 II) |

Cross-mount use requires adapters. For adapter products and compatibility rules bridging these mounts, see adapters.

# Canon EOS R5 Lens Compatibility

Canon EOS R5 lens compatibility: RF lenses fit natively, EF/EF-S lenses require Mount Adapter EF-EOS R, EF-M lenses are blocked (adapter does not support EF-M mount). Named pairings: RF 50mm f/1.8 STM (native), EF 50mm f/1.8 STM (adapter), EF-M 22mm f/2 STM (incompatible).

The Canon EOS R5 is a full-frame mirrorless camera (released 2020) with a Canon RF mount [1]. Lens compatibility breaks into three categories:

## RF Lenses — Native (direct fit)

RF-mount lenses mount directly to the EOS R5 with no adapter required. All electronic functions are fully supported [2].

**Example:** Canon RF 50mm f/1.8 STM — direct, no adapter needed [2].

## EF and EF-S Lenses — Adapter required

Canon EF and EF-S lenses are supported on the EOS R5 via the **Canon Mount Adapter EF-EOS R**. The EF/EF-S lens connects to the adapter, which connects to the camera's RF-side mount [3].

**Example:** Canon EF 50mm f/1.8 STM — requires Canon Mount Adapter EF-EOS R [3].

For adapter product details, see `adapters`.

## EF-M Lenses — Not compatible

EF-M lenses are **not supported** on the EOS R5. The Canon Mount Adapter EF-EOS R covers EF and EF-S lenses only; Canon does not document EF-M support through any adapter for the EOS R System [4].

**Example:** Canon EF-M 22mm f/2 STM — incompatible with EOS R5; do not recommend the EF-EOS R adapter for this lens [4].

# Lens Mount Standards

Definitions and specifications for mount standards (RF, EF, EF-M, etc.): physical dimensions, electronic interfaces, flange distance, and which camera systems use each mount

Three Canon lens mount standards are relevant to camera-lens compatibility: **EF**, **RF**, and **EF-M**.

## Canon EF Mount

The EF (Electro-Focus) mount is Canon's legacy interchangeable-lens standard used by Canon EF lenses and EF-S lenses [3]. It is a wide-diameter bayonet mount with fully electronic lens communication (no mechanical aperture linkage). EF is the mount found on Canon's DSLR bodies and is the source mount in Canon's EF-to-EOS R adapter ecosystem (see adapters for the Canon Mount Adapter EF-EOS R) [3].

## Canon RF Mount

The RF mount is Canon's mirrorless standard introduced with the EOS R system [1]. RF lenses attach to Canon EOS R-series mirrorless camera bodies [1]. The RF mount features a shorter flange distance and a wider 54 mm internal diameter compared to EF, enabling a high-speed communication bus between lens and body. RF lenses are not mechanically compatible with EF or EF-M bodies; bridging requires an adapter (see adapters).

## Canon EF-M Mount

The EF-M mount is Canon's mirrorless standard for the EOS M camera system [2]. It is a smaller-diameter mount designed for compact EOS M bodies, distinct from both EF and RF [2]. EF-M lenses (such as the EF-M 22mm f/2 STM) are native to EOS M cameras and are not directly compatible with EOS R bodies or EF-mount DSLRs without an adapter.

## Compatibility relationships

| Mount | System | Lens type | Directly compatible bodies |
|-------|--------|-----------|---------------------------|
| EF | EOS DSLR | EF, EF-S | EF-mount DSLRs (e.g., EOS 5D, 90D) |
| RF | EOS R (mirrorless) | RF | EOS R-series (e.g., R5, R6, R3) |
| EF-M | EOS M (mirrorless) | EF-M | EOS M-series (e.g., M50, M6 II) |

Cross-mount use requires adapters. For adapter products and compatibility rules bridging these mounts, see adapters.
